sentences.text: Revenue compounded at 1.5% a year from $41.9 billion in FY2016 to $47.9 billion in FY2025 [F219][F1][F10].
Operating income grew 5.3% a year and net income 8.1% a year, well ahead of revenue [F221][F222][F219].
Operating income jumped 37.7% to $13.8 billion in FY2025, mainly because other operating charges fell after the prior-year fairlife contingent consideration remeasurement [D450][F40][P12].
In FY2017 net income fell 80.9% to $1.25 billion as the effective tax rate hit 82.5%; the filings cited do not explain that rate [D44][F52][D28].
The US share of revenue rose to 39.9% in FY2025 from 31.4% in FY2019 [D523][D505].
In FY2025 North America added 1.5pp and EMEA 1.2pp to revenue growth of 1.9%, while Bottling Investments subtracted 1.0pp [D613][D636][D449][D597].
EMEA operating income rose to $4.30 billion on concentrate sales volume growth of 4% and favorable pricing [S50][P10].
Operating income grew 37.7% against revenue growth of 1.9%, an incremental margin of 428.4% [D450][D449][D473].
Diluted EPS compounded at 8.2% against net income at 8.1%, as diluted shares slipped from 4,367 million to 4,313 million [F224][F222][X116][X125].
Operating margin of 28.7% in FY2025 is the window high, against a median of 26.0% and a low of 20.7% [F50][D765][D766][D764].
The 7.5pp FY2025 gain came mostly from other lines (+6.2pp), with cost of revenue adding 0.6pp and SG&A 0.7pp [D463][D477][D475][D476].
Other lines improved because lower other operating charges followed the prior-year fairlife contingent consideration remeasurement [P12][D477].
In FY2024 other lines cut operating margin by 4.6pp within a 3.5pp net decline, which the filing attributes to higher other operating charges, commodity costs and refranchising [D427][D413][P25].
The window-high FY2025 margin is therefore largely a rebound from a charge, so it likely overstates underlying improvement [D477][D427].
Free cash flow of $5.30 billion was 0.40x net income in FY2025, the window low against a median of 0.97x [F120][D437][D776][D778].
That ranks in the 0th percentile among six staples peers, whose median is 0.94x [D795][D796].
Operating cash flow fell 41.3% in FY2024, mainly on the $6.0 billion IRS Tax Litigation Deposit [D404][P22].
Capex of $2.11 billion was 4.4% of revenue and 2.01x D&A, against 1.27x in FY2016 [F110][D432][D438][D11].
Cash and equivalents were $10.3 billion in FY2025, down 5.2%, and the 1.46x current ratio is the window high against a 1.13x median [F160][D469][F200][D780][D781].
Total debt shows $1,495 million for FY2025 against $41,716 million in FY2023, and the table carries no long-term debt line after FY2023 [D441][D340][F208].
Reported net cash of $8,775 million and its 100th percentile peer rank among six peers are therefore unreliable and support no conclusion [D442][D793].
Dividends of $8.78 billion and buybacks of $746 million took 179.9% of free cash flow, while diluted shares fell 0.2% [X145][X135][D445][D468].
Buybacks and dividends exceeded free cash flow in FY2023, FY2024 and FY2025, reaching 179.9% of it in FY2025 [R2][D344][D395][D445].
Free cash flow ran below 80% of net income in FY2024 and FY2025, at 0.45x and 0.40x, with FY2024 tied to the $6.0 billion IRS deposit [R3][D387][D437][P22].
The FY2025 10-K reports a $960 million fall in a trademark's fair value, leaving $2,440 million carrying value and likely further impairment if projections are missed [P20].
FY2017 and FY2018 revenue is recast at $36.2 billion and $34.3 billion, against $35.4 billion and $31.9 billion first reported; I draw no growth conclusions there [R1][F2][F3][X2][X3].
The 31.3% rise in total debt is dropped as an artefact of missing long-term debt lines, not a borrowing increase [R4][D470][D441][F208].
Free cash flow to net income staying at or below 0.40x would confirm weak conversion; a return toward the 0.97x median would reverse it, in the FY2026 10-K [D437][D778].
Operating margin falling below the 26.0% window median would show FY2025's 28.7% was charge-driven; holding above it would confirm durability, in the FY2026 10-K [D766][F50].
Any impairment reducing the $2,440 million trademark carrying value would confirm weaker projections; none would ease the concern, in the FY2026 10-K [P20].
